intro_cards.title: Pineal
body: Tiny, mid-brain. Melatonin — sleep / day-night clock.

intro_cards.title: Parathyroids
body: Four dots on the thyroid. PTH raises blood calcium (bone + kidney + gut).

intro_cards.title: Thymus
body: Behind the sternum, big in children. Trains T-lymphocytes. Shrinks with age.

intro_cards.title: Adrenals
body: Hats on the kidneys. Cortex: cortisol, aldosterone. Medulla: adrenaline (fight-or-flight).

units.title: The Skeletal System
units.intro: Bone is living: hard matrix (calcium salts) + collagen + cells. Compact bone outside, spongy inside, marrow in the middle (blood cells). Cartilage cushions; ligaments bone-to-bone.

cards.title: 3.1.1 Structure and Composition of Bone
body: A bone begins as cartilage before it is converted to bone through a process called ossification.
The key players in bone development are cartilage cells and mature bone cells.

cards.title: 3.1.2 Cartilage and Ligaments
body: Cartilage is a type of connective tissue consisting of a tough, flexible matrix made of collagen, protein, and sugar.
Although not as hard as a bone, cartilage forms an important structural component of many parts of the skeletal system.

cards.title: 3.1.3 Axial and Appendicular Skeletons
body: The axial skeleton encompasses the bones of the skull, vertebral column (backbone) and thorax (the sternum, or breastbone, and ribs).
The main function of the axial skeleton is to protect the vital organs of the body, such as the brain, heart and lungs, and to provide a structural framework that enables the body

cards.title: Skeletal system
body: Support, protection, movement (with muscles), mineral store, blood cell formation in marrow.
Bone types: long, short, flat, irregular. Joints: hinge, ball-and-socket, pivot…

cards.title: Bone growth & health
body: Calcium, vitamin D, exercise strengthen bones.
Osteoporosis: density loss risk in later life — prevention starts early.

cards.title: 3.2.1 Movable Joints
body: Ball-and-socket joint: The ball-shaped end of one bone fits into a cup-shaped socket on another.
The ball-and-socket joint allows movement in several directions, including rotation.

cards.title: 3.2.2 Immovable Joints
body: Immovable joints exist with bones that are in very close contact and are separated only by a thin layer of fibrous connective tissue.
Joints of the skull are extremely strong and immovable.
